name: Mimosa

project_scope.selection_mode: Genus Comparison Builder; canonical manifest plus live Master Plant Pool
source_concept_notes: Source-pool Mimosa aculeaticarpa var. biuncifera is already represented by canonical Mimosa biuncifera; do not create a duplicate.
Source-pool Mimosa quadrivalvis is not in the current canonical manifest. It is an installer/taxonomic identity dependency, not a sixth completed comparison card.
project_scope.range_policy: Preserve each species' existing native-range state; no range conclusions in this lesson.

shared_genus_traits: Leaves bipinnately compound, with each pinna divided into multiple small leaflets; inspect the rachis and pinna junctions rather than calling the leaf simply pinnate.
Inflorescences are dense, rounded heads of many small flowers whose conspicuous exserted stamens create the fuzzy appearance.
Fruits are legumes, often with specialized margins, constrictions or segments; mature pods can be more diagnostic than flower color.
Several species have pulvini and leaflets that respond to touch, but sensitivity is not unique to Mimosa and may be hard to observe in stressed or dried material.
look_here_first: First determine woody upright shrub versus prostrate/creeping perennial. Next count pinna pairs on several fully expanded leaves and inspect prickle position/curvature. For a confident species split, photograph a mature pod from the side, including its stalk, margins and constrictions.

quick_key.look: Woody shrub with persistent branched stems
Low sprawling or prostrate, herbaceous/creeping perennial
Usually 3–9 pairs of pinnae; 1–2 strongly recurved prickles near leaf nodes; pod often constricted between seeds
quick_key.confirm: Match node armature, pinna count and mature pod; the source-pool aculeaticarpa var. biuncifera concept is represented here.

quick_key.look: Grayish, relatively straight shoots; scattered less-curved prickles; usually 1–2 pinna pairs; longer stalked pod
quick_key.confirm: Compare stem prickle distribution and pod base against M. texana.

quick_key.look: Darker/zigzag shoots; strong downward-curving prickles; usually 1–4 pinna pairs; short, mostly unstalked pod
quick_key.confirm: Confirm mature pod and repeated leaf counts, not stem color alone.

quick_key.look: Prostrate creeping plant with conspicuously broad, prickly pod body that is not strongly pinched between seeds
quick_key.confirm: Pod body and margin are the strongest existing canonical cues.

quick_key.look: Sprawling sensitive-briar with up to about three pinna pairs and numerous small leaflets; mature pod not yet adequately characterized in the canonical record
quick_key.confirm: Do not assert separation from M. roemeriana until matched pod/armature characters are reviewed.

species_differences.first_check: Many pinna pairs on woody shoots
species_differences.confirm: Node-adjacent strongly recurved prickles and constricted mature pods
species_differences.caution: Pinna counts can overlap the upper end of M. texana; do not identify from flowers alone.

species_differences.first_check: Gray, straighter woody shoots and few pinna pairs
species_differences.confirm: Scattered prickles and longer stalked mature pods
species_differences.caution: Stem color is supporting evidence only; verify pod stalk and armature.

species_differences.confirm: Species-level pod and prickle characters await targeted review
species_differences.caution: Prostrate habit and touch-sensitive leaves overlap M. roemeriana; treat a flower-only observation as unresolved.

species_differences.confirm: Broad prickly mature pod with little constriction between seeds
species_differences.caution: Without fruit, the distinction from M. latidens remains provisional.

species_differences.first_check: Woody zigzag/darkish shoots with strong hooked prickles
species_differences.confirm: Few pinna pairs and shorter mostly sessile mature pods
species_differences.caution: M. borealis can overlap in foliage and habit; examine fruiting stems.

overlap_cautions: Pink or pale globose flower heads occur across these species; color is not a useful species separator.
Touch-sensitive leaflets also occur in related legumes and cannot independently identify a species.
Leaf pinna counts are ranges and should be scored on several mature leaves; juvenile or resprout foliage can mislead.
The low-growing M. latidens / M. roemeriana pair needs matched mature fruit, armature and leaf measurements before a hard dichotomous split.
The source-pool name M. aculeaticarpa var. biuncifera is already mapped to canonical M. biuncifera; do not reopen settled mapping.
M. quadrivalvis is a source-pool dependency, not a sixth canonical comparison species; avoid pretending this key covers it.

realistic_lookalikes.taxon: Desmanthus spp. (including D. illinoensis and D. leptolobus in source pool)
realistic_lookalikes.look: Bipinnate foliage and small round flower heads
realistic_lookalikes.separate: Inspect flower head details and especially mature narrow, often clustered legume pods rather than assuming a Mimosa pod.

realistic_lookalikes.look: Sensitive-looking bipinnate foliage and rounded flower clusters
realistic_lookalikes.separate: Compare inflorescence architecture and mature fruit; touch response is not decisive.
Examine inflorescence arrangement and full mature pods; do not rely on a single thorn or leaflet.

realistic_lookalikes.look: Fine bipinnate foliage and pale rounded flower clusters
realistic_lookalikes.separate: Use flower-head construction, stem armature and mature legumes to confirm genus.

Matched same-scale woody shoots for M. biuncifera, M. borealis and M. texana with node, prickle origin, orientation and ruler
Matched fully expanded leaves with labeled pinna-pair and leaflet-pair counts; several leaves per woody species
diagnostic_photo_checklist.species: M. biuncifera / M. borealis / M. texana

diagnostic_photo_checklist.target: Mature intact pods side by side with millimeter scale; label constrictions, margins, seed positions and basal stalk
diagnostic_photo_checklist.species: M. biuncifera / M. borealis / M. texana
